question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-3X+5 \\  & ={X}^{2}-3X+5I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(D)={D}^{2}-3D+5I.$

Let's calculate ${D}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{2} & =D\cdot D \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(D):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(D) & ={D}^{2}-3D+5I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-3+5 & -3+9+0 \\ -1+3+0 & 3+0+5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
